rebuttal_or_critique: I remain steadfast in my assessment that the current policy stance must be maintained. While headline inflation has moderated to 3.54%, this is largely a reflection of transient factors. The persistence of food inflation at 5.42% is a clear signal that supply-side pressures remain potent and capable of unanchoring inflation expectations. With the economy exhibiting a positive output gap of 0.30% and robust GVA growth of 6.80%, there is no evidence of a growth-inflation trade-off that warrants easing. Monetary policy must remain vigilant against the risk of inflation rebounding; shifting to a neutral stance or cutting rates prematurely would be a policy error that undermines our commitment to the 4.00% target. I cannot support a shift in stance until the disinflationary process is proven to be durable and immune to the volatility inherent in food and global commodity prices.
